articles.headline: Your Mindset About Getting Older Just Added Years
articles.body: <cite index="1-3,1-4">Research from Stanford shows that beliefs about aging directly influence health outcomes. People with more positive views of aging live longer by as much as 7.5 years and engage more readily in health-promoting behaviors.</cite> This isn't motivation theater. It's biology. <cite index="1-9">A holistic vision of longevity is built on relationships, resilience, movement and meaning.</cite> The gap between people who thrive and people who decline often starts in the mind.
articles.takeaway: Shift from "I'm getting older" to "I'm building resilience." Your nervous system believes the story you tell it.

articles.topic: AI predicts disease risk from sleep patterns
articles.headline: Your Sleep Just Became a Health Forecast
articles.body: <cite index="15-3,15-4">Researchers developed SleepFM, a multimodal sleep foundation model trained on over 585,000 hours of sleep recordings from 65,000 participants, which produces latent sleep representations that enable accurate prediction of future disease risk.</cite> Translation: one night of sleep data can signal trouble months or years before symptoms show. <cite index="15-5">This foundation model learns the language of sleep from multimodal recordings, enabling scalable, label-efficient analysis and disease prediction.</cite> Your sleep quality is now intelligence.
articles.takeaway: Quality sleep isn't a luxury—it's early warning. Protect it like the diagnostic tool it actually is.

articles.topic: Brain training improves cognition at any age
articles.headline: Cognitive Decline Isn't What Happens Next. It's What You Allow
articles.body: <cite index="19-1">A three-year study of brain health from UT Dallas suggests mental acuity does not inevitably diminish with age, and cognitive abilities can improve at any stage of life.</cite> <cite index="22-1,22-2">Adults who regularly engaged with digital brain-health training over three years showed measurable gains in cognitive, emotional, and social well-being, with nearly 4,000 adults showing measurable cognitive improvements tied to targeted training strategies.</cite> Five to 15 minutes a day. That's the dose. The rest is choice.
articles.takeaway: Your brain's plasticity doesn't expire. Small, consistent training now rewires the systems you'll need at 70.
articles.source: UT Dallas Center for BrainHealth / Scientific Reports

articles.topic: How the brain responds to stress determines resilience
articles.headline: Stress Doesn't Break You. Your Brain's Wiring Does
articles.body: <cite index="48-4,48-5,48-6,48-7">New research from Florida International University shows stress resilience isn't a flatline—it's a flex. Assistant professor Marcelo Bigliassi explored how the brain's internal wiring and a person's subjective experience of stress interact to determine how they respond to stressful situations.</cite> <cite index="48-8">These findings were recently published in the Journal of Applied Physiology.</cite> What matters isn't the pressure you face. It's how your nervous system interprets the signal.
articles.takeaway: You can't control external stress, but you can retrain how your brain responds to it. That's where your power actually lives.
articles.source: Florida International University / Journal of Applied Physiology

workout.title: Row, Hang, and Brace: Upper-Back Starter
equipment: pull-up bar or sturdy door frame
workout.tip: No pull-up bar? Use a resistance band anchored in a door for all row variations. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of each rep, not just pulling with your arms.
workout.warmup: Start with 60 seconds of arm circles (forward and back), 10 slow cat-cows on all fours, and 30 seconds of dead bug holds lying on your back. This wakes up the spine and activates the shoulder girdle before any pulling.

exercises.name: Dead Hang
exercises.notes: Hang from a bar with a shoulder-width grip, arms straight, shoulders packed down away from your ears. Breathe steadily. If a full hang is too hard, bend your knees and put light pressure through your feet on a chair.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Seated Row
exercises.notes: Anchor a band at mid-torso height. Sit tall, pull the band to your lower ribs, elbows close to your sides. Pause for one second at the end, then control the return. Do not round your back.

exercises.name: Scapular Pull-Up
exercises.notes: Hang from the bar with arms straight. Without bending your elbows, shrug your shoulder blades down and together to elevate your chest a few inches. Lower slowly. This builds the foundation for full pull-ups.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Face Pull
exercises.notes: Anchor the band at face height. Hold both ends with palms facing in, pull toward your forehead while flaring your elbows wide. Great for shoulder health and posture. Keep your core braced.

exercises.name: Plank with Alternating Shoulder Tap
exercises.notes: Hold a forearm or high plank. Tap one shoulder at a time while keeping your hips completely still. Slow and controlled beats fast and wobbly every time. Widen your feet if you need more stability.

workout.cooldown: Finish with a 60-second doorway chest opener stretch and a 60-second child's pose with arms extended. Let your shoulders fully drop and breathe into your upper back.

meal.title: Date & Cashew Butter Energy Bites
meal.description: No-bake bites made from Medjool dates, cashew butter, and a pinch of cinnamon—pure carb and fat fuel in handheld form. Endurance athletes love these for reliable energy that's easy to digest 45 minutes before a long effort.
meal.instructions:
1. Remove pits from dates and chop roughly.
2. Blend or food-process dates and cashew butter until sticky and well combined.
3. Fold in cinnamon and salt.
4. Roll into 6 equal balls (approximately 2 bites per ball).
5. Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days.
meal.tip: Make a full batch on Sunday—grab one 30–45 minutes before any endurance session. Dates are nature's performance fuel; the natural sugars digest fast without the artificial taste of most energy gels.
